Abstract

Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has gained substantial consideration in management circles and has been linked to Human Resource Management (HRM) in various ways. The study on how CSR would affect HRM or vice versa has been of interest by many scholars. However, much of the research has focused on developing the conceptual framework and theoretical constructs that can explain the relationship between the two. Although much work has been done on conceptualizing the relationship, empirical studies remain very scanty and the available empirical studies suffer from several weaknesses such as limited coverage of different dimensions of CSR and HRM, use of outdated theories, low sample size, poor methodological approaches, among others. This paper was originally aimed at filling these gaps. It examined how Corporate Social Responsibility impacts Human Resource Management practices in manufacturing firms in the southern part of Malaysia. A total of 160 questionnaires were distributed to a sample of 103 respondents from 27 firms using stratified random sampling technique and data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results show that the dimensions of CSR which includes the environmental aspect significantly and positively influences the training and development aspect of HRM. Therefore, we recommend that Malaysian manufacturing firms should take more cognizance of their corporate social responsibilities especially in terms of the environmental dimension and they should incorporate it into their human resource management practices so as to make them better firms to be in.

A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis* by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization. This is the first time that astaxanthin diglucoside diesters have been found in snow algae.

Abstract:
Leibowitz and his colleagues found that accommodation rests at an intermediate distance that shows wide interindividual variation. They proposed that this intermediate dark focus is useful for correcting anomalous refractive errors, but this proposal was later questioned when different measurement techniques yielded contradictory results. In the present study, we sought to develop a mathematical model that could accurately predict optimal accommodative performance from measures of the dark focus of accommodation, and thereby provide a theoretical framework for Leibowitz's theory of dark focus. The model was tested on a sample of 150 adults, aged 22-73, who performed a visual acuity test at each eye separately. The results of the study indicate that the model can accurately predict optimal accommodative performance from measures of the dark focus of accommodation, thus providing support for Leibowitz's theory of dark focus and showing how it can be used in clinical practice.

Abstract

The family is a social institution that is fundamental to the development of children into mature adults. Traditional family values are important to the development of an individual's values, beliefs and sense of identity, and have also been shown to play a role in the stability of the family as a unit. In light of the recent decline of family traditions and traditions being passed on to succeeding generations, the present study explores the following: (a) What are some common family traditions that were observed in previous generations? (b) How do those traditions contribute to the health and well-being of the family as a unit? and (c) How can we preserve and pass them down to the next generation?

This paper uses the case of Chinese families to explore how traditional Chinese family values and family traditions may be affecting the stability of the family today. There has been a lot of evidence that suggests that the family is becoming a less stable structure now than it was in the past, this may be because people are living longer and families are having fewer children, but the reasons are beyond the scope of this paper.

To conduct the study, a survey was given out to a randomly selected sample of 1000 Chinese men and women who are between the ages of 18-59 and married. The results showed that many families no longer keep the traditions their parents or grandparents had and that most respondents feel that this is a negative change from what their parents did.

It is recommended that in order to preserve family traditions, the whole family should be involved in creating them and keeping them up. Children, grand children, great grand children etc. should all be included in activities like cooking dinner, cleaning the house, decorating the house, going fishing, planting trees, reading books or watching movies together.

Key words: Intergenerational Transmission, Family Traditions, Generations, Family, Values

Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) mediate distinct biological responses by stimulating similar intracellular signaling pathways.
